The evidence suggests that Palivizumab targets the High affinity immunoglobulin gamma Fc receptor I, which in turn is a target of midostaurin and cetuximab. These compounds, in turn, target the Low affinity immunoglobulin gamma Fc region receptor III-B. This chain of targets implies a potential mechanism where Palivizumab may exert its effects by modulating the activity of the High affinity receptor, which could influence the downstream signaling of the Low affinity receptor. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible role for Palivizumab in regulating the function of the Low affinity receptor, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
